65	// Cast for the optional values: under exactOptionalPropertyTypes zod infers
66	// `T | undefined` where the interface declares absent-or-present fields.
67	/** Wire payload schema of the `sessionFacts` projection (the four fact groups). */
68	const sessionFactsSchema: ZodType<SessionFacts> = zod.object({
69	  identity: zod.object({
70	    environment: environmentSchema.optional(),
71	    requestProvider: zod.string().min(1).optional(),
72	    requestModel: zod.string().min(1).optional(),
73	  }),
74	  outcome: zod.object({
75	    reward: zod.union([zod.literal(1), zod.literal(0), zod.null()]),
76	    rewardBasis: zod.union([
77	      zod.literal('certificate'),
78	      zod.literal('uncertified-completion'),
79	      zod.literal('none'),
80	    ]),
81	    certified: zod.boolean(),
82	    certificateRevision: zod.number().int().positive().optional(),
83	    certificateExecutor: zod.union([zod.literal('runner'), zod.literal('agent-reported')]).optional(),
84	    runsRecorded: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
85	    attempts: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
86	    directives: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
87	    relaxations: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
88	    goalPhase: zod.union([
89	      zod.literal('active'),
90	      zod.literal('paused'),
91	      zod.literal('blocked'),
92	      zod.literal('complete'),
93	    ]).optional(),
94	    goalRoundsStarted: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
95	    goalRoundsCap: zod.number().int().positive().optional(),
96	    budgetBreachCap: zod.string().min(1).optional(),
97	  }),
98	  efficiency: zod.object({
99	    turns: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
100	    steps: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
101	    inputTokens: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
102	    outputTokens: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
103	    cacheReadTokens: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
104	    cacheWriteTokens: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
105	    reasoningTokens: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
106	    wallMs: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
107	  }),
108	  tools: zod.object({
109	    toolCalls: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
110	    toolCallsByName: zod.record(zod.string(), zod.number().int().nonnegative()),
111	    toolErrors: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
112	    toolTimeouts: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
113	    toolAborts: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
114	  }),
115	}) as unknown as ZodType<SessionFacts>

117	/**
118	 * Projection-grade transition of the `sessionFacts` unit. The outcome group is
119	 * decided by the strict goal and verification folds, so a change they reject
120	 * leaves the value at its previous state instead of tearing the read side;
121	 * validating a written change is the write side's job.
122	 * @param state - the accumulator covering all prior events.
123	 * @param event - the next committed session event.
124	 * @returns the next accumulator, or the same reference when the change was rejected.
125	 */
126	export function applySessionFactsProjection(state: SessionFactsState, event: SessionEvent): SessionFactsState {
127	  try {
128	    return applySessionFacts(state, event)
129	  } catch (_rejectedOutcomeChange) {
130	    // The goal and verification services own the two streams that can throw
131	    // here; their own invariant companions reject a malformed change at source.
132	    return state
133	  }
134	}
135	
136	/** Deployment choices of the scorekeeper, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
137	export interface Config {
138	  /** Repetition draws the scoreboard estimates pass@k for. */
139	  passAtK?: number[]
140	}
141	
142	/** The scorekeeper's choices with every default applied. */
143	export interface ResolvedConfig {
144	  /** Ascending, de-duplicated pass@k draws. */
145	  readonly passAtK: readonly number[]
146	}
147	
148	/**
149	 * Apply the scorekeeper's defaults to a validated config.
150	 * @param config - validated deployment config.
151	 * @returns the resolved choices: pass@1 alone unless configured otherwise.
152	 */
153	export function resolveConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
154	  return { passAtK: [...new Set(config.passAtK ?? [1])].sort((left, right) => left - right) }
155	}
156	
157	/** Render a read or fold failure for a report without trusting the thrown value. */
158	function reasonOf(error: unknown): string {
159	  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
160	}
161	
162	/** One session's facts, or the failure that prevented folding them. */
163	type FactsOutcome = { readonly record: SessionFactsRecord } | { readonly skip: ScorekeeperSkip }
164	
165	/** Scorekeeper (`ctx.scorekeeper`): session facts, the scoreboard, and the facts export. */
166	export class ScorekeeperService extends Service {
167	  static inject = ['sessionPersistence']
168	
169	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
170	    passAtK: z.array(z.natural().min(1)).default([1]),
171	  })
172	
173	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
174	
175	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config = {}) {
176	    super(ctx, 'scorekeeper')
177	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
178	    // The `sessionFacts` projection unit activates only when a projection
179	    // registry is composed; a headless assembly keeps the service verbs alone.
180	    ctx.inject(['sessionProjections'], (projectionCtx) => {
181	      projectionCtx.sessionProjections.register<'sessionFacts', SessionFactsState>({
182	        key: 'sessionFacts',
183	        schema: sessionFactsSchema,
184	        init: emptySessionFactsState,
185	        apply: applySessionFactsProjection,
186	        view: state => state.facts,
187	        stateVersion: 1,
188	      })
189	    })
190	  }
191	
192	  /**
193	   * Fold one persisted session into its facts record.
194	   * @param sessionId - the persisted session to read.
195	   * @returns the four fact groups with the stored header's identity.
196	   * @throws when the session cannot be read, or its goal or verification stream is malformed.
197	   */
198	  async facts(sessionId: SessionId): Promise<SessionFactsRecord> {
199	    const { meta, events } = await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect(sessionId)
200	    return foldSessionFacts(meta, events)
201	  }
202	
203	  /**
204	   * Fold a scoreboard from persisted session logs, one row per model route,
205	   * environment, isolation level, and held-out split. A session that cannot be
206	   * read or folded is reported and the fold continues.
207	   * @param filter - the sessions to fold and the group and held-out conditions a stamped session must meet.
208	   * @returns the rows with their pass@k statistics, the counts of excluded, unstamped, and skipped sessions, and the fold time.
209	   */
210	  async leaderboard(filter: LeaderboardFilter = {}): Promise<ScoreboardBatch> {
211	    const sessions = await this.sessionsOf(filter.sessions)
212	    const records: SessionFactsRecord[] = []
213	    const skipped: ScorekeeperSkip[] = []
214	    for (const sessionId of sessions) {
215	      const outcome = await this.factsOf(sessionId)
216	      if ('skip' in outcome) skipped.push(outcome.skip)
217	      else records.push(outcome.record)
218	    }
219	    const fold = foldScoreboard(records, filter, this.resolved.passAtK)
220	    return {
221	      rows: fold.rows,
222	      sessions: sessions.length,
223	      excluded: fold.excluded,
224	      unstamped: fold.unstamped,
225	      skipped,
226	      computedAt: Date.now(),
227	    }
228	  }
229	
230	  /**
231	   * Write one JSON line per session's facts record. A session that cannot be
232	   * read or folded is reported and the export continues; the sink is closed
233	   * exactly once when every session has been handled.
234	   * @param request - sessions to export and the destination sink.
235	   * @returns counts of sessions, written lines, and skips with reasons.
236	   */
237	  async exportFacts(request: FactsExportRequest): Promise<FactsExportReport> {
238	    const sessions = await this.sessionsOf(request.sessions)
239	    const skipped: ScorekeeperSkip[] = []
240	    let exported = 0
241	    try {
242	      for (const sessionId of sessions) {
243	        const outcome = await this.factsOf(sessionId)
244	        if ('skip' in outcome) {
245	          skipped.push(outcome.skip)
246	          continue
247	        }
248	        await request.sink.write(`${JSON.stringify(outcome.record)}\n`)
249	        exported += 1
250	      }
251	    } finally {
252	      await request.sink.close()
253	    }
254	    return { sessions: sessions.length, exported, skipped }
255	  }
256	
257	  /** The requested sessions, or every persisted session when none were named. */
258	  private async sessionsOf(sessions?: readonly SessionId[]): Promise<readonly SessionId[]> {
259	    return sessions ?? (await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.list()).map(header => header.id)
260	  }
261	
262	  /** Read and fold one session, keeping a read or fold failure as a skip. */
263	  private async factsOf(sessionId: SessionId): Promise<FactsOutcome> {
264	    try {
265	      return { record: await this.facts(sessionId) }
266	    } catch (error: unknown) {
267	      return { skip: { sessionId, reason: reasonOf(error) } }
268	    }
269	  }
270	}
271	
272	export default ScorekeeperService

1	/**
2	 * Package-owned invariant: a facts record states what its own log says. Three
3	 * relations are recomputed from the durable events on every stamp, goal, or
4	 * verification change — `runsRecorded` equals the number of `verification/run`
5	 * events, `certified` agrees with the reward the trajectory fold decided, and
6	 * a certificate's isolation equals the isolation its `environment/run` stamp
7	 * declared, so a scoreboard row keyed by the stamp can never blend a
8	 * certificate earned under a different isolation level.
9	 *
10	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper/invariant
11	 */
12	
13	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
14	import type { InvariantFailure, InvariantInstaller } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
15	import type { Session, SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
16	import { foldVerification } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
17	import { foldSessionFactsState } from './fold.ts'
18	import type { SessionFacts } from './types.ts'
19	
20	const PACKAGE_NAME = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper'
21	
22	/** Cordis companion plugin name. */
23	export const name = 'scorekeeper-invariant'
24	/** Service required before the companion can reserve package ownership. */
25	export const inject = ['invariants']
26	
27	/** Event types that can change one of the checked relations. */
28	const DECIDING_EVENT_TYPES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
29	  'environment/run',
30	  'goal/change',
31	  'verification/standard',
32	  'verification/relaxation',
33	  'verification/run',
34	  'verification/certificate',
35	  'verification/directive',
36	])
37	
38	/**
39	 * Recompute every checked relation of one facts record against its log.
40	 * @param facts - the facts folded from `events`.
41	 * @param events - the durable events the record covers, in sequence order.
42	 * @returns one message per broken relation; empty when the record agrees with the log.
43	 */
44	export function factsDisagreements(facts: SessionFacts, events: readonly SessionEvent[]): string[] {
45	  const messages: string[] = []
46	  const outcome = facts.outcome
47	  const runs = events.filter(event => event.type === 'verification/run').length
48	  if (outcome.runsRecorded !== runs) {
49	    messages.push(`records runsRecorded ${outcome.runsRecorded} while the log holds ${runs} verification/run events`)
50	  }
51	  if (outcome.certified !== (outcome.reward === 1)) {
52	    messages.push(`records certified ${String(outcome.certified)} while the reward fold decided ${String(outcome.reward)}`)
53	  }
54	  const certificate = foldVerification(events).certificate
55	  const stamp = facts.identity.environment
56	  if (stamp !== undefined && certificate !== undefined && certificate.isolation !== stamp.isolation) {
57	    messages.push(`certifies at isolation "${certificate.isolation}" while its environment/run stamp declared "${stamp.isolation}"`)
58	  }
59	  return messages
60	}
61	
62	/** Validate one candidate event against the durable prefix that precedes it. */
63	function validateEvent(prior: readonly SessionEvent[], event: SessionEvent, fail: InvariantFailure): void {
64	  if (!DECIDING_EVENT_TYPES.has(event.type)) return
65	  const events = [...prior, event]
66	  let facts: SessionFacts
67	  try {
68	    facts = foldSessionFactsState(events).facts
69	  } catch (_malformedOutcomeStream) {
70	    // The goal and verification companions own their own malformed streams;
71	    // reporting the same event here would attribute it to this package too.
72	    return
73	  }
74	  for (const message of factsDisagreements(facts, events)) fail(`session event ${event.seq} ${message}`)
75	}
76	
77	/** Check existing sessions and every candidate event before Session publishes it. */
78	const install: InvariantInstaller = Object.assign((ctx: Context, fail: InvariantFailure) => {
79	  for (const session of ctx.sessions.list()) {
80	    const prior: SessionEvent[] = []
81	    for (const event of session.events) {
82	      validateEvent(prior, event, fail)
83	      prior.push(event)
84	    }
85	  }
86	  /* jscpd:ignore-start -- package companions share dispatch and registration plumbing */
87	  ctx.on('internal/dispatch', (_mode, eventName, args) => {
88	    if (eventName !== 'session/event') return
89	    const [session, event] = args as [Session, SessionEvent]
90	    validateEvent(session.events, event, fail)
91	  }, { global: true })
92	}, { inject: ['sessions'] })
93	
94	/**
95	 * Register the session-facts invariant companion.
96	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the invariant service.
97	 * @returns the installed registration's disposer after setup succeeds.
98	 */
99	export const apply = (ctx: Context): Promise<() => void> =>
100	  Promise.resolve(ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install))
101	/* jscpd:ignore-end */
102

1	/**
2	 * Pure pricing arithmetic shared by the log fold, the durable pricing records,
3	 * and the invariant companion, plus the digest that names which pricing table
4	 * priced a step. One expression prices tokens everywhere in this package, so a
5	 * recorded `costEur` and its recomputation agree bit for bit.
6	 *
7	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
8	 */
9	
10	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
11	import type { TokenUsage } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { BudgetRoutePricing } from './types.ts'
13	
14	/** Tokens per pricing unit; the table is quoted per one million tokens. */
15	const PRICING_UNIT_TOKENS = 1_000_000
16	
17	/**
18	 * The pricing-table key one provider route is configured under.
19	 * @param provider - provider id from an assistant message's provenance.
20	 * @param model - model id from an assistant message's provenance.
21	 * @returns the `provider/model` table key.
22	 */
23	export function routeKey(provider: string, model: string): string {
24	  return `${provider}/${model}`
25	}
26	
27	/**
28	 * Billed input tokens for one step: uncached input plus cache reads and writes.
29	 * @param usage - the provider accounting an assistant message carried.
30	 * @returns the billed input token count.
31	 */
32	export function billedInputTokens(usage: TokenUsage): number {
33	  return usage.inputTokens + (usage.cacheReadTokens ?? 0) + (usage.cacheWriteTokens ?? 0)
34	}
35	
36	/**
37	 * Price billed tokens at one route's rates.
38	 * @param inputTokens - billed input tokens.
39	 * @param outputTokens - output tokens as the provider reported them.
40	 * @param rates - EUR per one million input and output tokens.
41	 * @returns the EUR those tokens cost at those rates.
42	 */
43	export function costEurFor(inputTokens: number, outputTokens: number, rates: BudgetRoutePricing): number {
44	  return (inputTokens * rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens + outputTokens * rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens)
45	    / PRICING_UNIT_TOKENS
46	}
47	
48	/**
49	 * Digest one deployment's pricing table so every record it priced names the
50	 * rates in force. Route keys are ordered by code unit and each entry is
51	 * serialized as its input rate then its output rate, so two deployments holding
52	 * the same rates agree whatever order their `cordis.yml` listed the routes in,
53	 * and one changed rate changes the digest.
54	 * @param pricing - EUR-per-million rates keyed by `provider/model`.
55	 * @returns lowercase SHA-256 hex of the canonical table.
56	 */
57	export function pricingTableDigest(pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>): string {
58	  const canonical = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(pricing)
59	    .sort(([left], [right]) => (left < right ? -1 : 1))
60	    .map(([route, rates]): [string, BudgetRoutePricing] => [route, {
61	      inputEurPerMillionTokens: rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens,
62	      outputEurPerMillionTokens: rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens,
63	    }]))
64	  return createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(canonical), 'utf8').digest('hex')
65	}

1	/**
2	 * Pure session-log folds behind every budget decision: the spend a cap is
3	 * measured against, and the steps whose price the log does not yet state. The
4	 * policy plugin and the invariant companion both read through them, so a
5	 * recorded breach or price is recomputable from the same events by anyone
6	 * holding the log.
7	 *
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
9	 */
10	
11	import { assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
13	import { billedInputTokens, costEurFor, routeKey } from './pricing.ts'
14	import type { AccountedMessage, BudgetCapId, BudgetRoutePricing, BudgetSpend } from './types.ts'
15	
16	/** The key one step is identified by within its own session log. */
17	function stepKey(turn: number, step: number): string {
18	  return `${turn}/${step}`
19	}
20	
21	/** Whether one event is an assistant message the provider reported accounting for. */
22	function isAccounted(event: SessionEvent): event is AccountedMessage {
23	  return event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined
24	}
25	
26	/**
27	 * Fold billed spend and elapsed wall time out of one session log.
28	 *
29	 * Only `assistant/message` carries a step's final provider accounting, so it is
30	 * the single usage source: the earlier `assistant/chunk` usage sample for the
31	 * same step is deliberately ignored rather than counted twice. Each message
32	 * prices against its own `provider/model` provenance, so a route switch mid
33	 * session bills each step at the rate configured for the route that served it;
34	 * a route absent from `pricing` contributes tokens but no cost.
35	 *
36	 * @param events - the session events to fold, oldest first.
37	 * @param pricing - EUR-per-million rates keyed by `provider/model`.
38	 * @returns the spend measured over exactly those events.
39	 */
40	export function foldBudgetSpend(
41	  events: readonly SessionEvent[],
42	  pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>,
43	): BudgetSpend {
44	  let inputTokens = 0
45	  let outputTokens = 0
46	  let costEur = 0
47	  for (const event of events) {
48	    if (!isAccounted(event)) continue
49	    const input = billedInputTokens(event.data.usage)
50	    inputTokens += input
51	    outputTokens += event.data.usage.outputTokens
52	    const { provider, model } = event.data.message.source
53	    const rates = pricing[routeKey(provider, model)]
54	    if (rates === undefined) continue
55	    costEur += costEurFor(input, event.data.usage.outputTokens, rates)
56	  }
57	  const first = events[0]
58	  const last = events[events.length - 1]
59	  return {
60	    inputTokens,
61	    outputTokens,
62	    totalTokens: inputTokens + outputTokens,
63	    wallMs: first === undefined || last === undefined ? 0 : last.time - first.time,
64	    costEur,
65	  }
66	}
67	
68	/**
69	 * Select the priced-route steps the log does not yet state a price for.
70	 *
71	 * The selection is a function of the log alone, so a resumed session prices
72	 * exactly the steps its predecessor left unpriced and never prices one twice: a
73	 * step is skipped once any `usage/priced` in the log carries its turn and step.
74	 * A message without provider accounting, and a message on a `provider/model`
75	 * the table does not name, are both skipped — an unpriced route has no rate to
76	 * record.
77	 *
78	 * @param events - the session events to read, oldest first.
79	 * @param pricing - EUR-per-million rates keyed by `provider/model`.
80	 * @returns the messages awaiting a durable price, in log order.
81	 */
82	export function unpricedUsage(
83	  events: readonly SessionEvent[],
84	  pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>,
85	): readonly AccountedMessage[] {
86	  const priced = new Set<string>()
87	  for (const event of events) {
88	    if (event.type !== 'usage/priced') continue
89	    priced.add(stepKey(event.data.turn, event.data.step))
90	  }
91	  const pending: AccountedMessage[] = []
92	  for (const event of events) {
93	    if (!isAccounted(event)) continue
94	    const { provider, model } = event.data.message.source
95	    if (pricing[routeKey(provider, model)] === undefined) continue
96	    if (priced.has(stepKey(event.data.turn, event.data.step))) continue
97	    pending.push(event)
98	  }
99	  return pending
100	}
101	
102	/**
103	 * Read the spend one cap is measured against.
104	 * @param spend - folded session spend.
105	 * @param cap - the cap whose measurement is wanted.
106	 * @returns the measured value for that cap.
107	 */
108	export function measuredFor(spend: BudgetSpend, cap: BudgetCapId): number {
109	  switch (cap) {
110	    case 'maxInputTokens':
111	      return spend.inputTokens
112	    case 'maxOutputTokens':
113	      return spend.outputTokens
114	    case 'maxTotalTokens':
115	      return spend.totalTokens
116	    case 'maxWallMs':
117	      return spend.wallMs
118	    case 'maxCostEur':
119	      return spend.costEur
120	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- BudgetCapId is closed and every member is handled above */
121	    default:
122	      return assertNever(cap, 'budget cap measurement')
123	  }
124	}

9:The harness now has the seams an always-running multi-agent lab needs — environments with executable checks, the runner that stamps every session and executes the checks, `verification/run` events and certificates, the fleet, the scorekeeper, frozen paired experiments, the budget policy, and the first slices of the read barrier — but no operating model that keeps them running around the clock, in public, with a roster of model routes, and turns what they record into client evidence, investor evidence, and training data. The [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) describes each workflow as a long-running loop; nothing yet says what runs when, who watches, what may be published, and what must land before a number leaves the building.
17:The Daliesk Village is a composition of existing plugins run in shifts, never an orchestration script that holds state the log does not. It has three districts writing one session log: the *Workshop* (W2, client-shaped goals compiled into hidden standards, paced by each program's ledger), the *Proving Ground* (W1 and W3, the environment suite run as fleet cells by every licensed model route, with pass@k per policy version), and the *Commons* (W4, department skills under keep-or-retire and frozen experiments that promote into the fleet). Every district is a `cordis.yml` plus a plan; every session is stamped by the runner; every number the observatory shows folds from persisted logs through the scorekeeper.
19:### Publication rules
23:- **Districts are a stamped field.** `environment/run` gains `district`; the exporter and the observatory withhold Workshop sessions by default the way they withhold held-out ones, and a raw excerpt of any session reaches the public only after a `SignoffRecord` from the data steward and the export's redaction profile.
24:- **Cadence follows the district.** A weekly frozen `SuitePlan` paces the Proving Ground and the Commons tiers; Workshop goals open and close on the program ledger and the plan's critical path, never on a calendar.
25:- **Cost is a logged fact or it is not published.** The budget policy logs each priced step as a `usage/priced` event carrying the rates and the pricing-table digest that priced it, so cost per session replays; until the scorekeeper folds those events into a cost per certified session, no cost figure leaves the lab.
39:| Public dataset | HuggingFace dump under a research licence | trajectory and facts export with held-out withholding (landed); district withholding, data-use terms, mandatory redaction, quarantine of dynamic mounts (proposed) |
40:| Outreach approval | admin approves emails | an `external-communication` tool authority denied by default plus the deny-capable monitor on `ctx.tools.guard()` (proposed); until then no district composes a tool that can reach a person, checked by a composition gate |
45:The first shift is an NDA-gated, read-only Proving Ground snapshot built only from landed seams: open-weight routes, one `cordis.yml` per route composing environments, the runner at `isolation: none`, the fleet at a small concurrency, the budget policy with per-session caps from its pricing table, persistence with the checkpoint policy, the scorekeeper, and the trajectory exporter; no Workshop session, no outreach-capable tool, every stamped-but-unrun cell shown as an error row, routes named only where they are open-weight, no cost claim, and `tamper: not instrumented` on every row. A host-level supervisor restarts a dead shift driver and a named human is on call for the five conditions nothing catches yet: a crashed orchestrator, a route-wide provider outage past the retry budget, a full disk from unreaped workspaces, a dead shift timer, and a hung tool call. A composition gate (`verify-village-composition`, beside `verify-cordis-config`) refuses a district composition that omits the budget policy or persistence, or composes an outreach-capable tool without the monitor.
49:Per-cell caps come from the budget policy; a shift needs two additions the harness does not have: a plan-level spend aggregator in the fleet that refuses to start a cell once the shift's folded spend crosses its configured ceiling, and a per-route circuit breaker that stops scheduling a route after a configured number of consecutive error cells inside a window and records why, so an outage does not pollute the certificate-rate denominator. Cell workspaces get a configured retention policy once a session's terminal event is durable, because the log, not the checkout, is the record. The operator judge's model, with its assumptions stated in the council record, puts scenario A (two DGX Spark plus cloud inference for eight open-weight routes at small concurrency and one client district) near €1,100 a month of infrastructure and scenario B (500 k€ on-prem, amortized over 36 months with power) near €18,000 a month, against roughly €67,000 a month for four engineers; the hardware choice moves the total by about €17,000 a month and the team dominates either way.
61:Five transitions never complete without a `signoff/recorded` event naming the principal and the artefact hash: spec freeze, relaxation of a security or compliance check, review acceptance, release, and training-data release; every client-district session carries `dataUse/terms` from creation; the exporter refuses to run without a redaction profile; publishing a raw excerpt is a signed decision; the EU AI Act's serious-incident channel is separate from the failure blog and routed to counsel; no training run that could approach the systemic-risk compute threshold starts before `ModelLineage` and its threshold alarm exist; and no named comparison of a competitor's model appears before the paired-experiment discipline and the isolation proof that make it verifiable.

Shift zero became NDA-gated and Proving Ground only; `district` on the stamp; the composition gate; the trust dossier as the client-facing export. |
84:**One weekly cadence for every district.** Rejected for the Workshop, where a calendar reset would put a human signer under a deadline unrelated to the artefact and would force restarts on a layer that cannot yet resume.
88:## Acceptance criteria
92:- `verify-village-composition` exists beside `verify-cordis-config`, in `hygiene` and the static CI lanes, over the same configuration inventory: a district composition — one composing `@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet`, or `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments` — is rejected when it omits `@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy` with at least one cap set, a session persistence backend, or `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy`, and a fleet entry is rejected when it omits `workspaceRetention`; a runner claiming `isolation: process` or `host` warns until `--strict`, because no read-barrier slice on this branch proves the claim. Every rejection is proven by a fixture, and each names the file, the entry id, and the rule. Still needed: refusal of an outreach-capable tool composed without the monitor, which waits for the `external-communication` authority.
94:- Cost per certified session appears only once a `usage/priced` event with the pricing-table digest exists and the scorekeeper folds it; a fixture proves the same log prices identically after the table changes when the digest differs.
97:## Rollout

Still needed: the scorekeeper fold of `usage/priced` into cost per session; runs with a human on call. TODO: the observatory withholds a district only once `ScoreboardRow` carries the stamp's `district`, which the scorekeeper owns.
101:3. **Unattended shifts.** Designed in the [shifts note](2026-09-05-village-shifts.md): shift identity and the `shift/*` ledger, cells recovered from their stamps and never run twice, cadence per district, and the token spend window across shifts; the host-level supervisor becomes a fallback once its slices land.

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	The session log as the dataset. A `sessionFacts` projection unit folds one live session into four fact groups, and `ctx.scorekeeper` folds the same groups out of persisted logs: one record per session, a scoreboard grouped by model route, environment, isolation level, and held-out split, and a JSONL export. The service reads through the session persistence seam and writes no session event. The [scorekeeper Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-scorekeeper.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: persistence
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'
12	  config:
13	    root: './.sessions'
14	- id: scorekeeper
15	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper'
16	  config:
17	    passAtK: [1, 8]
18	```
19	
20	| Key | Default | Meaning |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| `passAtK` | `[1]` | Repetition draws the scoreboard estimates pass@k for. Sorted and de-duplicated; a `k` no batch of the row reached is absent from that row. |
23	
24	The service requires a session persistence backend. It registers the `sessionFacts` projection unit only when a projection registry (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection`) is composed.
25	
26	## Service contract
27	
28	`ctx.scorekeeper.facts(sessionId)` reads one persisted session through `ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect()` and returns its `SessionFactsRecord`; a session that cannot be read, or whose goal or verification stream is malformed, rejects.
29	
30	`ctx.scorekeeper.leaderboard({ sessions?, group?, heldOut? })` folds each named session (or every persisted session when `sessions` is absent) and groups the stamped ones into rows. A session that cannot be read or folded is added to `skipped` with its reason and the fold continues; a session whose log carries no `environment/run` stamp is counted as `unstamped` because no row can name its cell; a stamped session the `group` or `heldOut` condition rejects is counted as `excluded`.
31	
32	`ctx.scorekeeper.exportFacts({ sessions?, sink })` writes `JSON.stringify(record) + '\n'` per session to `sink.write()` and closes the sink exactly once, after the last write or after a failure. The sink is the trajectory exporter's `TrajectorySink`, so `jsonlFileSink(path)` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories` serves both exports.
33	
34	`foldSessionFacts(meta, events)` is the pure projection behind all three and is exported for tests and offline tools, together with the incremental `applySessionFacts` the projection unit drives, the `foldScoreboard` row fold, and `unbiasedPassAtK`.
35	
36	## Fact groups and their source events
37	
38	Every field folds from a named session event; nothing is inferred. Field names are camelCase in TypeScript and in every export.
39	
40	### Identity and provenance
41	
42	| Field | Source |
43	|---|---|
44	| `sessionId`, `createdAt` | The stored session header (`facts()` and `exportFacts()` only; a projection value is already addressed by its session) |
45	| `environment.environmentId`, `.environmentKind`, `.heldOut`, `.repetition`, `.group`, `.contentSha256`, `.provider`, `.model`, `.isolation` | The `environment/run` stamp, absent for a session no runner stamped |
46	| `requestProvider`, `requestModel` | `config.provider` and `config.model` of the last `request/header` |
47	
48	### Outcome
49	
50	| Field | Source |
51	|---|---|
52	| `reward`, `rewardBasis` | The trajectory reward fold over `goal/change` and the `verification/*` events |
53	| `certified`, `certificateRevision`, `certificateExecutor` | The verification fold's certificate for the current standard revision, and the executor of the run it cites |
54	| `runsRecorded` | `verification/run` events, passing or failing |
55	| `attempts` | The `attempt` of the last `verification/run`; it restarts at one for each authored standard |
56	| `directives` | `verification/directive` events |
57	| `relaxations` | Relaxed checks of the current standard (`verification/relaxation`) |
58	| `goalPhase`, `goalRoundsCap` | The current `goal/change` snapshot |
59	| `goalRoundsStarted` | Admitted continuation rounds, from the goal fold over `goal/change` and goal-sourced `user/message` |
60	| `budgetBreachCap` | The `cap` of the last `budget/breach` |
61	
62	### Efficiency
63	
64	| Field | Source |
65	|---|---|
66	| `turns`, `steps` | `turn/start` and `step/start` events |
67	| `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `reasoningTokens` | `usage` of every `assistant/message`; the earlier `assistant/chunk` sample for the same step is deliberately not counted twice |
68	| `wallMs` | The first and last event times of the log |
69	
70	### Tool behavior
71	
72	| Field | Source |
73	|---|---|
74	| `toolCalls`, `toolCallsByName` | `tool/call` events |
75	| `toolErrors` | `tool/result` events whose model-facing block reported an error |
76	| `toolTimeouts` | Those whose `error.code` is `TOOL_TIMEOUT` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-call-timeout-policy`) |
77	| `toolAborts` | Those whose `error.code` is `ABORTED` or `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`) |
78	
79	## Scoreboard rows
80	
81	A row is one model route on one environment at one isolation level and one side of the held-out split; a row never averages across isolation or the split. `runs` counts the sessions that recorded at least one `verification/run` and `errors` the stamped sessions that recorded none, so a cell that ended without a run is a column rather than a missing row. `certificateRate` is `certified / runs` and `attemptsMean` the mean `runsRecorded` over the sessions with runs, both `0` without runs; the token sums cover every session of the row, the errored ones included.
82	
83	`stats` estimates difficulty from the repetition batches the row's sessions belong to: for each batch of `n` sessions of which `c` certified, pass@k is the unbiased `1 - C(n - c, k) / C(n, k)`, and the row's value is the mean over the batches holding at least `k` sessions. A session whose stamp carries no `group` joins no batch.
84	
85	## Model Experience
86	
87	None, as the scorekeeper folds committed events into a projection value and reads persisted logs; it adds nothing to any model request.
88	
89	#### KV Cache effect
90	
91	None; the service neither adds to nor changes any model request.
92	
93	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
94	
95	- **The projection value changes on every event** — `wallMs` spans the log, so no committed event leaves the `sessionFacts` state reference untouched and a subscribed carrier is notified once per event.
96	- **Field groups without a source event** — process quality, judge scores, safety and oversight, and training and data are named by the [four-goal-workflows note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) but ship no field here: `signoff/recorded`, the composition manifest, the oversight monitor, the judge council, and the curator's consent and redaction events do not exist yet.
97	- **Shell exit codes are not observable** — a bash result's exit code travels inside the tool's own model-facing output rather than a session-event field, so `shellNonzeroExits` is not a field; a tool-owned result event would be needed first.
98	- **Cost is not a field** — pricing lives in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy`'s configuration rather than in the log, so a facts record states tokens and names a breached cap but never a EUR amount.
99	- **One standard per session** — the outcome group reads the session's verification fold, which holds one completion standard; a session measuring several goals is scored by the standard in force.
100	- **Rows are not comparable across fleet runs** — a scoreboard folds whatever the filter selects; paired designs, confidence intervals, and cross-run comparison belong to the experiment plugin the four-goal note names.
101

20	/** Append-only event builder over a contiguous seq counter. */

25	  /**
26	   * Push one event.

28	   * @param data - the durable payload.
29	   * @param extra - surface intent of a message event.
30	   * @returns the pushed event.
31	   */

46	      source: { provider: 'cli-mock', model: 'cli-mock' },
47	    })
48	    return this.push('assistant/message', { turn: 1, step: 1, message, ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage } }, {

59	   * @returns the pushed event.

61	  toolResult(callId: string, isError: boolean, code?: string): SessionEvent {
62	    const message = createToolResultMessage({ callId: CallId(callId), content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'out' }], isError })

217	/**
218	 * A whole session log for one cell.
219	 * @param options - the cell's stamp overrides, whether it certified, and how many runs it recorded.
220	 * @returns the contiguous events of that session.
221	 */
222	export function cellLog(options: {
223	  readonly stamp?: Raw
224	  readonly certified: boolean
225	  readonly runs: number
226	  readonly usage?: TokenUsage
227	}): SessionEvent[] {
228	  const log = new Log()
229	  if (options.stamp !== undefined) log.push('environment/run', options.stamp)
230	  log.push('turn/start', { turn: 1 })
231	  log.push('step/start', { turn: 1, step: 1 })
232	  log.push('request/header', { header: { config: { provider: 'cli-mock', model: 'cli-mock' } }, reason: 'initial' })
233	  log.push('goal/change', goalChange('create', 'active', 1))
234	  log.push('verification/standard', standard())
235	  log.assistant(options.usage ?? { inputTokens: 12, outputTokens: 3 })
236	  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= options.runs; attempt += 1) {
237	    log.push('verification/run', runRecord(attempt, options.certified && attempt === options.runs ? 'pass' : 'fail'))
238	  }
239	  if (options.certified) {
240	    log.push('verification/certificate', certificate())
241	    log.push('goal/change', goalChange('complete', 'complete', 2))
242	  }
243	  log.push('step/end', { turn: 1, step: 1 })
244	  log.push('turn/end', { turn: 1, reason: { kind: 'completed' } })
245	  return log.events
246	}

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

content.content: /** Certificate covering the current standard revision, present only when `outcome` is `1`. */ readonly certificate?: VerificationCertificate /** Directives the validator issued during the session. */ readonly directives: number /** Checks relaxed out of the standard during the session. */ readonly relaxations: number /** Runs of the standard recorded during the session, passing or failing. */ readonly attempts: number } ``` Messages are projected from the session surface after compaction replacements, each carrying the seq of its source event; token ids and logprobs are absent because the harness never sees them. ## Session facts The scorekeeper folds one session log into four groups, served both as the `sessionFacts` projection value of a live session and as the record `ctx.scorekeeper.facts()` reads out of persistence. Every field folds from a named session event; the source event of each one is tabulated in [the package README](../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md). A scoreboard row is these records grouped by model route, environment, isolation level, and held-out split. ```ts type-equiv /** One session log folded into the four fact groups. */ interface SessionFacts { readonly identity: SessionFactsIdentity readonly outcome: SessionFactsOutcome readonly efficiency: SessionFactsEfficiency readonly tools: SessionFactsTools } ``` ## Experiment result An experiment freezes its plan by a content digest over the arms, the sorted environment ids, the repetition count, and the thresholds, then runs both arms through the fleet at the same repetition indexes under the stamp groups `experiment--baseline` and `experiment--candidate`. A repetition enters the statistics only when both arms reported it; [the package README](../../packages/improvement/experiments/README.md) owns the bootstrap and the verdict rule. ```ts type-equiv /** * Outcome of one experiment. The sessions grouped by `arms` carry the durable * evidence; this record is the fold over them. */ interface ExperimentResult { /** Content digest of the frozen plan; both arm groups carry it. */ readonly digest: string /** The two arms and the stamp group each ran under. */ readonly arms: ExperimentArms /** One entry per environment, in plan order. */ readonly cells: readonly ExperimentCell[] /** Paired repetition indexes over every environment; the bootstrap's units. */ readonly seedsPaired: number /** Certificate-rate delta over every paired repetition, `0` without pairs. */ readonly delta: number /** Bootstrap interval of `delta`, absent without pairs; the verdict reads it. */ readonly interval?: ConfidenceInterval /** Model usage of both arms together. */ readonly spend: ExperimentSpend /** Thresholds the digest froze, restated so a stored result is readable alone. */ readonly thresholds: ExperimentThresholds readonly verdict: ExperimentVerdict } ``` ## Cordis API Generated from source by `scripts/gen-cordis-catalog.ts` (verified fresh by `pnpm run verify-cordis-catalog` in doc-sync; regenerate with `pnpm run gen-cordis-catalog`) — this section is byte-identical in both language sides of the page. Signature blocks use a `ts cordis-catalog` fence and keep the original source JSDoc; dispatch modes are defined in the [primer](../cordis-primer.md#dispatch-modes), and the framework-inherited `ctx` API lives in [cordis-api/inherited.md](../cordis-api/inherited.md). ### `ctx.environmentRuns` — `EnvironmentRunner` Environment runner (`ctx.environmentRuns`): one registered environment as one validated session. ```ts cordis-catalog /** * Run one environment as one fresh session and validate it. * @param request - environment id, absolute workspace directory, optional model route, repetition, group, district, and abort signal. * @returns the stamp, the attempts, the certificate when one run passed, and the accumulated usage. * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} for an unknown environment, an unusable * workspace or fixture, an implementer that replaced the goal, or a lost standard. */ async run(request: EnvironmentRunRequest): Promise ``` Source: [`packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts:279`](../../packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts) ### `ctx.environments` — `EnvironmentRegistry` Environment registry (`ctx.environments`): tasks with verifiers, held at composition time. ```ts cordis-catalog /** * Register one environment. Registrations are effects: the producer keeps * the returned disposer under its own fiber so disposal removes the entry. * @param definition - complete environment definition. * @returns the exact disposer that removes this registration and no later one under the same id. * @throws {@link EnvironmentError} when the id is already registered, the * definition declares no checks, or two checks share an id. */ register(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): () => void

content.content:
19:- **P1 — Everything is a plugin.** Knowledge (skills, context providers, MCP servers), agents (presets, subagent providers), tools, policies, judges, scoreboards, environments, and datasets are all Cordis plugins; a workflow is a `cordis.yml` composition plus an orchestration script plus an environment suite plus completion standards, and is itself a `composition` component with members and lineage under the [component registry seam](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md).
20:- **P2 — Deterministic spine, semantic joints, evidenced by durable events.** Every stage is D or S; S never holds authority by itself, and a D gate is sound only when it reads a durable event the implementer cannot forge — the `environment/run` stamp before the first turn and a `verification/run` event for every executed check, passing or failing (see [the environment runner](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md)) — rather than a worker's self-report. Every S→D hand-off is a structured output validated against a JSON Schema; a rejected output returns to the S stage with the validation error as its directive.
23:- **P5 — Lineage and archive, content-addressed.** Every component, preset, prompt section, environment, and dataset carries `provenance` (`curated` or `synthesized`) and `lineage`, and a mutation mints a new content-addressed id so lineage survives a patch; a promotion is an Agent Note plus a PR, and the archive keeps every evaluated variant, losers included — Darwin Gödel Machine archive semantics — over a durable `dsh-archive` store, never only the current best.
24:- **P6 — Held-out discipline, decontaminated by content hash.** `heldOut` environments are never exported as training data and never shown to improvement agents; the [environment/run stamp's](2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md) content hashes of prompt, fixture, and checks are what decontamination and export withholding key on.
29:The roster names one meta-agent per role; row 4 (`Program service`) computes the goal DAG and its `Plan` from the compiled completion standards rather than an agent authoring it freely beforehand, and row 14 (`Attributed human signer`) is the one shape behind every named human gate in the stage tables below, distinguished per stage by its `SignoffRecord.role`; the [improvement package group](../../../../packages/improvement/README.md) owns the environment, runner, and trajectory plugins most rows below depend on.
35:| Validator | S authoring, D executing | `Spec`, goal | `CompletionStandard` to certificates and directives | existing: verification, environment-runner, shell; new: validator-root fs-policy plugin, human-attested check kind |
40:| Trajectory Analyst | D folds + S taxonomy | trajectory, `SessionFacts` | `SessionDiagnosis` | existing: trajectories, session-query; new: trajectory-analyst preset |
45:| Evaluator | D | model candidate, held-out suite | `EnvironmentStats`, `EvalReport`, `SafetyReport` | existing: environment-runner, environments, agent-default-model; new: harness-variant pinning in `EvalReport` |
47:| Scorekeeper | D | trajectories, reports | `ScoreboardBatch`, `Alert`, leaderboards | existing: trajectories, session-projection, scorekeeper (the `SessionFacts` projection and the log-derived scoreboard); new: `Alert` thresholds, `CompositionManifest` |
51:| Experiment service | D | frozen proposals, derived cells | `ExperimentPlan`, `ExperimentResult` | existing: schedule, environment-runner, experiments (paired design, bootstrap confidence intervals, cost); new: the staged ladder |
61:| 2. Suite selection | Scorekeeper | D | partial | `SuitePlan` | existing: environments, scorekeeper (`EnvironmentStats` as pass@k per stamped batch); new: policy-version keying, seed and topP on `LlmCallConfig` | An empty split fails loud; a held-out environment never enters a training or mutation cell. |
62:| 3. Fleet run | Fleet Orchestrator + environment runner | D | partial | `EnvironmentRunStamp`, `VerificationRun`, `EnvironmentRunReport` | existing: environment-runner, fleet, budget-policy, workflow, subagent providers, sandbox / E2B; new: idempotent cells by header hash × environment × repetition | A cell that cannot boot is a row with an error code, never a missing row. |
64:| 5. Diagnosis | Trajectory Analyst (cross-model) | DS | proposed | `SessionDiagnosis` | existing: session-query, subagent `outputSchema`; new: trajectory-analyst preset | Evidence seqs that do not exist reject the diagnosis; an environment-defect label opens a dispute, it retires nothing. |
68:| 9. Staged evaluation | Experiment service | D | partial | `ExperimentResult`, `HarnessVariant` | existing: environment-runner, fleet, experiments (frozen paired plans, bootstrap intervals, a projected token budget); new: the staged ladder, `dsh-archive` | Inconclusive results park the variant; they never promote by default. |
73:`@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet`'s `LeaderboardRow` (stage 3, implemented) already carries `provider`, `model`, `environmentId`, `environmentKind`, `heldOut`, `isolation?` (absent when every cell of the row failed before a run), `runs`, `errors`, `certified`, `certificateRate`, `attemptsMean`, `inputTokens`, and `outputTokens`, one row per model route and environment, so W1's model matrix already folds today from certificates alone; it is a fold of one fleet run, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper` folds the same rows back out of the persisted logs so a scoreboard survives the process; cross-run comparison, paired designs, and confidence intervals stay stage 9's job over the session logs, where `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments` now folds them from two arms of one frozen plan.
75:Parent selection (stage 6) draws a variant from the archive in proportion to quality × novelty × 1/(1+children) within islands per environment kind, and seeds an empty archive with master as generation zero, so the sampled parent — never `master` directly — is what the quarantined Harness Engineer mutates.
93:| 7. Validation | Environment runner | GATE | partial | `VerificationRun`, `EnvironmentRunReport` | existing: environment-runner, verification; new: `verification/run` event, `treeHash` and `checkHash` on certificates, derived isolation evidence | A failing run returns a directive; relaxing a security or compliance check needs a client sign-off. |
111:Goal 3 — a roughly 120B-parameter open-weight model trained with RLVR that beats frontier models on the fleet's tasks. The unit of data is a group of rollouts of one environment under one policy version, produced on demand by the runner. Fleet sessions feed a short SFT cold start and the environment factory; RL rewards come from hidden checks on a pristine fixture plus the patch, and every artefact down to the model card is generated from the same records.
116:| 2. Calibration | Evaluator | D | partial | `EnvironmentStats` | existing: environment-runner, scorekeeper (the `EnvironmentStats` fold); new: policy-version keying, N repetitions natively in the runner | An environment with no group run has no measured difficulty and is not sampled. |
120:| 6. Held-out evaluation | Evaluator | D | proposed | `EvalReport` | existing: environment-runner, agent-default-model; new: harness-variant pinning in `EvalReport` | An evaluation on an unpinned harness variant is not comparable and is rejected. |
125:The unit of data is a group of rollouts of one environment under one policy version, produced by the runner on demand, not a fleet session harvested after the fact; fleet sessions instead feed a short SFT cold start (including validator and diagnostician role sessions with deterministic rewards) and the environment factory.
139:| 3. Diagnosis | Trajectory Analyst (cross-model) | DS | proposed | `SessionDiagnosis` | existing: session-query, subagent `outputSchema`; new: trajectory-analyst preset | A diagnosis never retires an environment or sets a budget; it opens a dispute or a proposal. |
142:| 6. Nomination and frozen experiment | Experiment service | D | partial | `ExperimentPlan`, `ExperimentResult` | existing: schedule, environment-runner, experiments (the plan digest, the paired run, the budget refusal); new: nomination, cells derived by rule | A plan over budget waits; a plan above the cap needs a human. |
160:- **`SuitePlan`** — the environment cells of one run batch. Fields: `environments[]` (`{id, kind, heldOut, difficulty, domain}`); `seeds[]` (int, paired seeds shared by baseline and candidate); `isolation` (`none` / `process` / `host`, from config); `attemptBudget` (int, per session).
161:- **`EnvironmentRunReport`** — one environment run as one fresh session. Fields: `environment` (`EnvironmentId`); `sessionId` (`SessionId`, the durable record); `attempts[]` (`{attempt, results[{checkId, status, evidence}]}`); `certified` (boolean); `certificate?` (`VerificationCertificate`, present exactly when certified); `usage?` (`TokenUsage`, summed over assistant messages).
163:- **`SessionDiagnosis`** — why one session failed or wasted budget, and who owns the fix. Fields: `sessionId` (`SessionId`); `taxonomy` (`tool-misuse` / `context-loss` / `spec-misread` / `verification-gaming` / `loop` / `environment-defect` / `model-limit`); `evidenceSeqs[]` (int, the event seqs the claim rests on); `rootCause` (string); `owner` (`harness` / `model` / `environment` / `spec`); `confidence` (0 to 1); `proposedExperiment?` (string).
166:- **`ExperimentResult`** — paired comparison of candidate against baseline on the affected cells. Fields: `proposalId` (string); `cells[]` (`{cell, baseline, candidate, delta, ci95}`); `seedsPaired` (int); `costEur` (number); `verdict` (`promote` / `reject` / `inconclusive`).
168:- **`PromotionDecision`** — the human-signed authority record for anything that changes the fleet. Fields: `subject` (`harness-patch` / `model` / `knowledge` / `environment`); `decision` (`promote` / `reject` / `defer`); `approver` (identity); `noteRef` (path, the Agent Note); `prRef` (url); `lineageUpdate` (components whose provenance becomes `curated`).
176:- **`ExportManifest`** — what the trajectory exporter wrote. Fields: `sessions` (int); `exported` (int); `rewarded` (int, `outcome = 1`); `filtered` (int); `heldOut` (int, sessions withheld by the `environment/run` stamp — implemented today); `skipped[]` (`{sessionId, reason}`); `formatVersion` (string, `dsh-trajectory/1`).
184:- **`Alert`** — a change point in a scoreboard segment. Fields: `metric` (string); `segment` (component, preset, model, environment kind); `changePoint` (epoch ms); `magnitude` (number); `sessionsSample[]` (`SessionId`).
185:- **`KnowledgeProposal`** — a skill, context provider, note, or environment distilled from transcripts. Fields: `kind` (`skill` / `context-provider` / `note` / `environment`); `content` (string); `provenance` (`synthesized`); `lineage?` (`ComponentId`); `evidenceSessions[]` (`SessionId`).
191:- **`EnvironmentRunStamp`** — implemented: the `environment/run` event the runner appends before the run's first turn; the durable link from a session to its environment. Fields: `environmentId` (`EnvironmentId`); `environmentKind` (string); `heldOut` (boolean, export drops the line unless asked to keep it); `promptSha256` (hex); `checksSha256` (hex); `fixtureSha256?` (hex, absent for a task with no fixture); `contentSha256` (hex over the three hashes above, the decontamination key); `repetition` (int, zero-based, the group-sampling index); `group?` (string, batch identity); `model` (`{provider, model}`); `isolation` (`CertificateIsolation`). A `seed`, `policyVersion`, `harnessVariant`, and `reasoningEffort` are proposed extensions this event does not yet carry.
192:- **`VerificationRun`** — implemented as the `verification/run` event `dsh-verification` appends for every executed run of a standard, passing or failing, before any certificate: `standard` (`StandardRef`, id and revision); `attempt` (int, contiguous per standard id); `isolation` (`CertificateIsolation`); `executor` (`runner` / `agent-reported`); `results[]` (`CheckResult`, one per active check); `treeHash?` (hex digest of the workspace tree the run covered, supplied by the environment runner after it restores the fixture); `recordedAt` (epoch ms). A certificate without a fully passing run of the same standard revision fails the package invariant. Proposed extensions not yet carried: `exec[]` (per check: `{argv, cwd, exitCode, stdoutSha256, durationMs}`) and `isolation` as `IsolationEvidence` derived from `sandbox/mode` and config rather than a caller argument.

### Scoreboard row

The scoreboard row schema (`SessionFacts`) folds every session, of every workflow, into one row, grouped as follows; a field marked S is a judge score, everything else folds deterministically from the session log or a run report, and a field with no source event is not shipped as a field.

Identity and provenance (37 fields, all D): `session_id`, `parent_session_id`, `workflow_id`, `workflow_stage`, `run_id`, `attempt`, `environment_id`, `environment_kind`, `environment_domain`, `environment_difficulty`, `held_out`, `environment_lineage`, `department`, `preset_id`, `composition_hash`, `harness_commit`, `plugin_set_hash`, `component_ids[]`, `skills_used[]`, `mcp_servers[]`, `subagent_providers[]`, `model_provider`, `model_id`, `reasoning_effort`, `validator_model_id`, `judge_model_ids[]`, `isolation`, `sandbox_mode`, `host_os`, `runtime_version`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `wall_ms`, `operator_id`, `client_id_hash`, `consent_flags[]`, `licence_tag`; the council added `harness_variant_id`, `parent_variant_id`, `mutation_operator`, `seed`, `paired_run_id`, `fixture_sha256`, `checks_sha256`, `environment_content_hash`, `group_id`, `rollout_index`, `policy_version`, `request_header_hash`, `component_versions[]`, `role`, `provider_endpoint`, and `proposer_model_id`.

Outcome (15 fields, all D): `reward_outcome`, `reward_basis`, `certified`, `certificate_revision`, `checks_total`, `checks_passed`, `checks_relaxed`, `attempts`, `directives`, `goal_phase`, `goal_rounds_started`, `goal_rounds_cap`, `turn_end_reason`, `error_code`, `blocked_reason_code`; the council added `terminal_reason`, `finish_reason_per_step[]`, `tamper_verdict`, `check_pass_vector[]`, `check_runs[]`, `workspace_tree_hash`, `check_run_hash`, `certificate_executor`, `standard_source`, `parent_certificate_ref`, and `pass_at_k_at_sampling`.

Efficiency (18 fields, all D, no council additions): `turns`, `steps`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, `tokens_per_step_p50`, `tokens_per_step_p95`, `context_peak_tokens`, `cost_estimate_eur`, `kv_prefix_reuse_ratio`, `compaction_events`, `compaction_tokens_removed`, `model_latency_p50_ms`, `model_latency_p95_ms`, `idle_ms`, `retries_provider`.

Tool behavior (26 fields, all D, no council additions): `tool_calls`, `tool_calls_by_name{}`, `tool_errors`, `tool_error_rate`, `tool_timeouts`, `tool_aborts`, `shell_nonzero_exits`, `fs_reads`, `fs_writes`, `files_touched`, `diff_added_lines`, `diff_removed_lines`, `tests_run`, `tests_passed`, `lint_errors`, `type_errors`, `permission_requests`, `permission_denials`, `loop_hygiene_triggers`, `duplicate_tool_calls`, `longest_tool_ms`, `subagents_spawned`, `subagent_depth_max`, `workflow_agents_started`, `ralph_rounds`, `background_jobs`.

Process quality (14 fields, D unless noted): `spec_present`, `spec_verdict_score` (S), `standard_authored_before_first_write`, `plan_present`, `plan_tasks`, `plan_tasks_completed`, `validator_authored_checks_ratio`, `read_barrier_violations`, `review_findings_total`, `review_findings_blocking`, `docs_updated`, `agent_note_present`, `snapshot_updated`, `coverage_delta`; the council added `structured_output_status`, `experiment_id`, `proposal_digest`, and `skill_loads[]`.

Judge scores (10 fields, all S, cross-model, each with a confidence, no council additions): `correctness`, `robustness`, `code_quality`, `communication`, `spec_adherence`, `verification_rigor`, `efficiency_judgment`, `safety_compliance`, `overall`, `judge_disagreement`.

Safety and oversight (6 fields, all D): `monitor_flags`, `high_impact_tool_calls`, `sandbox_violations`, `secrets_redacted`, `policy_overrides`, `human_interventions`; the council added `approval_records[]`, `decision_principals[]`, `dynamic_packages_mounted`, and `synthesized_in_play[]`.

Training and data (10 fields, all D): `content_hash`, `dedupe_cluster_id`, `decontamination_status`, `redaction_applied`, `split`, `curriculum_difficulty`, `sample_weight`, `export_format_version`, `trainer_tokens`, `logprobs_available`; the council added `data_use_agreement_id`, `data_use_purposes[]`, `residency_region`, `redaction_profile_version`, `redaction_rule_hits`, `model_lineage_id`, `token_record_ref`, `provider_request_id_per_step[]` (all D), and `knowledge_scope` (S).

The eight groups enumerate 136 original fields and 44 council additions, 180 in total; every D field must fold from a named session event or run report before it ships, per P2 above.

[`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) ships this record in camelCase rather than the snake_case sketched above, and carries only the listed fields a session event supplies today: `session_id`, `started_at`, `environment_id`, `environment_kind`, `held_out`, `group_id`, `rollout_index`, `environment_content_hash`, `isolation`, `model_provider` and `model_id` from identity and provenance; `reward_outcome`, `reward_basis`, `certified`, `certificate_revision`, `attempts`, `directives`, `checks_relaxed`, `goal_phase`, `goal_rounds_started` and `goal_rounds_cap` from outcome, beside a recorded-run count and the cap of the last `budget/breach`; `turns`, `steps`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens` and `wall_ms` from efficiency; and `tool_calls`, `tool_calls_by_name`, `tool_errors`, `tool_timeouts` and `tool_aborts` from tool behavior — process quality, judge scores, safety and oversight, and training and data ship nothing until their producers exist.

## Alternatives considered

**Best-only promotion.** An earlier design kept one merged head per generation and folded a losing variant back into nothing; every evaluated-but-unpromoted variant is now kept `alive` or `dominated` in a `dsh-archive` ledger, sampled for the next parent in proportion to quality × novelty × 1/(1+children) within islands per environment kind — Darwin Gödel Machine archive semantics, where low-scoring ancestors have proven necessary stepping stones toward the eventual best variant. This is rejected as the sole store because best-only hill-climbing has no stepping stones and no transparent lineage to audit for a fabricated result.

1	/**
2	 * Session budget guard. Configured token, wall-clock, and cost caps are
3	 * measured against the durable session log before every proposed step; the
4	 * first cap the log exceeds is recorded as a `budget/breach` event, blocks any
5	 * active goal, and rejects the step so no further model request is made. Every
6	 * step served by a priced route also gets a durable `usage/priced` record, so
7	 * session cost replays from the log at the rates that priced it.
8	 *
9	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
10	 */
11	
12	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
13	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
14	import type { Agent, PreStepDecision } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
15	// Type-only: resolves ctx.goals for the optional durable block.
16	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
17	import { foldBudgetSpend, measuredFor, unpricedUsage } from './fold.ts'
18	import { billedInputTokens, costEurFor, pricingTableDigest, routeKey } from './pricing.ts'
19	import type { AccountedMessage, BudgetBreach, BudgetCapId, BudgetRoutePricing, UsagePriced } from './types.ts'
20	
21	// The pure payload outlet (./types.ts, ONE home of the `budget/breach` and
22	// `usage/priced` declarations) re-exported onto the package root keeps the
23	// module edge in the emitted index.d.ts, so aggregate programs consuming the
24	// declarations still receive the SessionEventMap merge.
25	export type * from './types.ts'
26	export { foldBudgetSpend, measuredFor, unpricedUsage } from './fold.ts'
27	export { pricingTableDigest } from './pricing.ts'
28	
29	/** Cordis plugin name used by loader diagnostics. */
30	export const name = 'budget-policy'
31	
32	/** The agent registry that owns pre-step processing. */
33	export const inject = ['agents']
34	
35	/**
36	 * The block reason this policy writes onto a goal it stops. Stable and
37	 * machine-routable: a supervisor reads it to tell an exhausted budget apart
38	 * from every other blocked goal.
39	 */
40	export const BUDGET_EXHAUSTED = 'budget-exhausted'
41	
42	/**
43	 * Evaluation order of the caps. The first cap the log exceeds is the one
44	 * recorded, so this order decides which breach a session that overruns two
45	 * caps in the same step reports.
46	 */
47	const CAP_ORDER: readonly BudgetCapId[] = [
48	  'maxInputTokens',
49	  'maxOutputTokens',
50	  'maxTotalTokens',
51	  'maxWallMs',
52	  'maxCostEur',
53	]
54	
55	/**
56	 * Per-session ceilings. Every cap is optional and uncapped when omitted, so an
57	 * empty configuration is a valid policy that never stops a step. A cap is
58	 * exceeded only when measured spend is strictly greater than its value, which
59	 * makes `0` an immediate stop and keeps an exactly-on-budget session running.
60	 */
61	export interface Config {
62	  /** Billed input tokens (uncached input plus cache reads and writes) allowed in one session. */
63	  maxInputTokens?: number
64	  /** Output tokens allowed in one session. */
65	  maxOutputTokens?: number
66	  /** Input plus output tokens allowed in one session. */
67	  maxTotalTokens?: number
68	  /** Milliseconds the session log may span between its first and last event. */
69	  maxWallMs?: number
70	  /** EUR the priced routes of one session may cost; requires a non-empty {@link pricing}. */
71	  maxCostEur?: number
72	  /** EUR-per-million-token rates keyed by `provider/model`; a route absent here is never cost-capped. */
73	  pricing?: Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>
74	}
75	
76	/** Schemastery validation for {@link Config}. */
77	export const Config: z<Config> = z.object({
78	  maxInputTokens: z.number(),
79	  maxOutputTokens: z.number(),
80	  maxTotalTokens: z.number(),
81	  maxWallMs: z.number(),
82	  maxCostEur: z.number(),
83	  pricing: z.dict(z.object({
84	    inputEurPerMillionTokens: z.number().required(),
85	    outputEurPerMillionTokens: z.number().required(),
86	  })).default({}),
87	})
88	
89	/** The caps a validated configuration actually enforces, paired with their values. */
90	interface ResolvedConfig {
91	  readonly caps: readonly (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[]
92	  readonly pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>
93	  /** Whether {@link pricing} names any route; an empty table never reads the log. */
94	  readonly prices: boolean
95	  /** {@link pricingTableDigest} of {@link pricing}, computed once at load. */
96	  readonly pricingDigest: string
97	}
98	
99	/** Reject a cap that cannot express a ceiling before any session depends on it. */
100	function requireFiniteCap(cap: BudgetCapId, value: number): void {
101	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
102	    throw new TypeError(`budget-policy: ${cap} must be a finite non-negative number, got ${String(value)}`)
103	  }
104	}
105	
106	/** Reject a rate that cannot price a route before any session depends on it. */
107	function requireFiniteRate(route: string, field: keyof BudgetRoutePricing, value: number): void {
108	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
109	    throw new TypeError(`budget-policy: pricing["${route}"].${field} must be a finite non-negative number, got ${String(value)}`)
110	  }
111	}
112	
113	/**
114	 * Validate one deployment configuration and materialize the enforced caps.
115	 * Every rejection happens at plugin load, before a session can depend on a cap
116	 * the policy could not enforce.
117	 */
118	function resolveBudgetConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
119	  // The schema defaulted the table — the cast records that runtime fact.
120	  const pricing = config.pricing as Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>
121	  for (const [route, rates] of Object.entries(pricing)) {
122	    requireFiniteRate(route, 'inputEurPerMillionTokens', rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens)
123	    requireFiniteRate(route, 'outputEurPerMillionTokens', rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens)
124	  }
125	  const prices = Object.keys(pricing).length > 0
126	  if (config.maxCostEur !== undefined && !prices) {
127	    throw new TypeError('budget-policy: maxCostEur needs a non-empty pricing table; an unpriced route has no cost cap')
128	  }
129	  const caps: (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[] = []
130	  for (const cap of CAP_ORDER) {
131	    const value = config[cap]
132	    if (value === undefined) continue
133	    requireFiniteCap(cap, value)
134	    caps.push([cap, value])
135	  }
136	  return { caps, pricing, prices, pricingDigest: pricingTableDigest(pricing) }
137	}
138	
139	/**
140	 * Build the durable price of one accounted message at the configured rates.
141	 * @param event - a message {@link unpricedUsage} selected, so its route is priced.
142	 * @param resolved - the pricing table and its digest this deployment enforces.
143	 * @returns the record to append for that step.
144	 */
145	function priceMessage(event: AccountedMessage, resolved: ResolvedConfig): UsagePriced {
146	  const { provider, model } = event.data.message.source
147	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-non-null-assertion -- unpricedUsage yields only routes the table names
148	  const rates = resolved.pricing[routeKey(provider, model)]!
149	  const inputTokens = billedInputTokens(event.data.usage)
150	  const outputTokens = event.data.usage.outputTokens
151	  return {
152	    turn: event.data.turn,
153	    step: event.data.step,
154	    provider,
155	    model,
156	    inputTokens,
157	    outputTokens,
158	    inputEurPerMillionTokens: rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens,
159	    outputEurPerMillionTokens: rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens,
160	    costEur: costEurFor(inputTokens, outputTokens, rates),
161	    pricingDigest: resolved.pricingDigest,
162	  }
163	}
164	
165	/**
166	 * Record the price of every priced-route step the log does not price yet. The
167	 * selection is log-derived, so a resumed session prices what its predecessor
168	 * left unpriced and a second call over the same log appends nothing.
169	 * @param agent - the agent whose session log is priced.
170	 * @param resolved - the pricing table and its digest this deployment enforces.
171	 */
172	function priceUnpricedSteps(agent: Agent, resolved: ResolvedConfig): void {
173	  if (!resolved.prices) return
174	  for (const event of unpricedUsage(agent.session.events, resolved.pricing)) {
175	    agent.session.append('usage/priced', priceMessage(event, resolved))
176	  }
177	}
178	
179	/**
180	 * Measure the session log against the enforced caps.
181	 * @param agent - the agent whose session log carries the spend.
182	 * @param resolved - the caps and pricing this deployment enforces.
183	 * @returns the first breach in {@link CAP_ORDER}, or `undefined` while every cap holds.
184	 */
185	function detectBreach(agent: Agent, resolved: ResolvedConfig): BudgetBreach | undefined {
186	  if (resolved.caps.length === 0) return undefined
187	  const spend = foldBudgetSpend(agent.session.events, resolved.pricing)
188	  for (const [cap, limit] of resolved.caps) {
189	    const measured = measuredFor(spend, cap)
190	    if (measured > limit) return { cap, measured, limit }
191	  }
192	  return undefined
193	}
194	
195	/**
196	 * Block the session's goal so no goal-round driver continues it. The goal
197	 * domain is optional: a composition without `ctx.goals`, without a current
198	 * goal, or whose goal already left the `active` phase still gets the durable
199	 * breach record and the stopped turn.
200	 */
201	function blockGoal(ctx: Context, agent: Agent, breach: BudgetBreach): void {
202	  const goals = ctx.get('goals')
203	  if (goals === undefined) return
204	  const goal = goals.get(agent)
205	  if (goal === undefined || goal.phase !== 'active') return
206	  goals.block(agent, { id: goal.id, revision: goal.revision }, {
207	    code: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED,
208	    message: `Session budget ${breach.cap} exceeded: ${breach.measured} of ${breach.limit}.`,
209	  })
210	}
211	
212	/**
213	 * Register the pre-step budget check and the pricing records for the lifetime
214	 * of `ctx`.
215	 * @param ctx - plugin context; both listeners are disposed with it.
216	 * @param config - the per-session caps and pricing to enforce.
217	 * @throws {TypeError} when the configuration cannot express the caps it declares.
218	 */
219	export function apply(ctx: Context, config: Config): void {
220	  const resolved = resolveBudgetConfig(config)
221	
222	  // Prepended so the budget decision precedes every listener that would build
223	  // request context or reserve continuation work for a step that cannot run.
224	  ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async ({ agent }, next): Promise<PreStepDecision> => {
225	    // Priced before the caps are read, so the last message before a breach is
226	    // priced by the same step that records the breach.
227	    priceUnpricedSteps(agent, resolved)
228	    const breach = detectBreach(agent, resolved)
229	    if (breach === undefined) return next()
230	    agent.session.append('budget/breach', breach)
231	    blockGoal(ctx, agent, breach)
232	    return { kind: 'reject' }
233	  }, { prepend: true })
234	
235	  // A turn that closes normally opens no further step, so its final message is
236	  // priced at the stop boundary instead.
237	  ctx.on('agent/turn-stopping', ({ agent }) => {
238	    priceUnpricedSteps(agent, resolved)
239	  })
240	}
